description: Deterministic rules used by the correlation engine. 'signature_rules' turn Suricata alerts, Zeek notices, Wazuh host alerts and AMiner anomalies into semantic tags; 'technique_rules' turn tags into ATT&CK mappings. Every rule is validated against attack_catalog.json at load time.

signature_rules.pattern: (?i)sudo to root|first time user executed sudo|\bsu(do)?\b.*root|privilege escalation
(?i)multiple web server 400 error codes|attempt to access forbidden (file|directory)
(?i)aminer: .*apache access (request|log)|aminer: new (request method|status code|characters) in apache
(?i)web_server|web application attack|sql injection|xss|web shell|common web attack|suspicious url access

technique_rules.reason: One source contacted many hosts with failed/short connections (address sweep).
A high rate of connections from one source to one TCP service is consistent with vulnerability scanning or crawling.
Many destination ports probed on the same host, or a scan signature fired.
Repeated failed SSH authentications between the same pair of hosts.
Bursts of connections from one source to the same authentication-capable service (e.g. admin console, SMB, RDP, FTP) are consistent with password guessing; conn records do not show login results.
A successful login followed many failures; a guessed valid account is plausible but network data cannot prove the account was misused.
An internal host reached several internal hosts over remote-administration protocols; consistent with lateral movement but also with administration tooling.
A web-attack signature fired; it shows an attempt, not successful exploitation.
An IDS signature for known C2 TLS/HTTP traffic matched this flow.
Regular, low-jitter outbound connections are consistent with beaconing, but also with legitimate agents.
Long, high-entropy DNS labels to one domain are consistent with DNS tunnelling.
Data could be leaving inside DNS queries; the payload content is not visible.
A large internal-to-external transfer may be exfiltration; the transfer alone does not prove data theft.
Bursts of HTTP 4xx errors / forbidden-path requests from one client against one web server (host logs) are typical of wordlist scanners such as dirb or WPScan.
The log-anomaly detector saw new request methods, status codes or characters in a web server's access log; consistent with vulnerability scanning but also with new legitimate clients.
Repeated authentication failures were logged by the target host for one source / service within an hour.
The host logged a root-level sudo/su execution. It can be administration; together with earlier attack stages it indicates privilege escalation.
New user/credential parameter combinations appeared in the audit log; consistent with privilege changes but not proof of them.
High-entropy / unusual characters in queried DNS names can carry exfiltrated data; also seen with CDNs and tracking domains.
